cim: Your guide to AI degrees and certificates in Utah
cim_eredeti: Your guide to AI degrees and certificates in Utah
szoveg_eredeti:
As artificial intelligence has revolutionized everything in every industry, Utah universities have responded in kind by creating new certificate and degree programs to prepare students to implement AI across multiple sectors. From St. George to Logan, Utahns can find programs that connect AI to engineering, data science, business, writing, teaching and healthcare.

Please note: All course lengths demonstrate the estimated completion time and thus might vary for each student. Consequently, tuition fees are subject to change depending on the year. Also, every degree and program will have a variety of requirements before enrolling in the course (e.g., be in a certain program, have a completed bachelor’s degree, etc.), so please keep that in mind when looking at the following options.

Bachelor of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence & Data Engineering

Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence Engineering

Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence for Business

Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence

What students have to say: “My degree taught me much more than just how to use AI tools. It gave me a better understanding of how artificial intelligence and machine learning actually work, from preparing and analyzing data to training models, evaluating their results, and understanding their limitations. … I now have a much broader range of directions I can take my career. I can still pursue traditional software development, but I can also look toward AI and machine learning, data-focused roles, AI integration, automation and positions where software development and AI overlap.” — Alex Turro, a recent graduate with a Master of Applied AI.

Master of Business Administration — Business Artificial Intelligence Emphasis

Bachelor of Science in Artificial Intelligence

Master of Science or Ph.D. in Computing — AI Track

AI and Writing — certificate (undergraduate)

Remote Sensing and Geospatial AI Foundations — certificate (undergraduate)

Applied Remote Sensing and Geospatial Artificial Intelligence — post-bachelor’s certificate

Master in Applied Machine Learning and Statistics

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Certificate

Post-Baccalaureate Certificate in Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

What students have to say: “For me, it’s been a really empowering experience. Specifically, [I’ve gained] a deeper understanding of how to build and evaluate datasets and models, guiding me both on a macro level of what machine learning and AI tooling I use, and in making small adjustments to the models I use. … I’ve personally focused on models in subject matters that I find personally interesting like speech and music, and discovered there was still so much to learn in these subjects when you take another look through a more data-focused lens.” — Zach Walton, a second-year student in the Master of Artificial Intelligence program.

Applied Artificial Intelligence, Undergraduate Certificate

Applied AI in Organizations, Undergraduate Certificate

Bachelor of Science in Information Systems — Applied Artificial Intelligence Emphasis

Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence

Artificial Intelligence, Graduate Certificate

What students have to say: “In a world being constantly changed by AI, my education at UVU gave me a chance to engage with new and emerging technologies, including AI and other topics that I have found essential in my professional career. Being able to learn about AI before it became mainstream allowed me to quickly adapt and utilize it in my professional work and the college courses that I teach, better preparing our future generations for anything that may come their way.” — Noah Say, a 2021 UVU graduate with a Bachelor of Science in Information Systems and currently an Applied AI instructor.

Computational Data Science and Machine Learning Graduate Certificate

Weber State University has also proposed Associate and Bachelor of Science degrees in Computer Science and AI. If approved by the Utah System of Higher Education, these stackable degrees will provide students with “advanced theoretical and mathematical foundations in computer science and artificial intelligence,” according to proposals provided by News Coordinator Alexis Cirkovic.

Master of Science in Computer Science — AI and Machine Learning Specialization

Master of Science in Software Engineering — AI Engineering Specialization

In addition to its degree programs, Western Governors University offers several AI-related certificates: AI and Machine Learning Developer Certificate, AI Skills Fundamentals Certificate, AI Strategy for Business Certificate, AI Fundamentals in Healthcare Certificate, AI for K-12 Teachers Certificate and AI for K-12 Education Leaders Certificate.

What students have to say: “Traditional software engineering is rapidly transitioning toward AI engineering, and WGU’s hands-on curriculum gave me the exact framework and confidence to make that leap. The coursework directly supports my current role leading the development of agentic tooling to power our AI at Adobe. Understanding model evaluations and transformer architecture is critical in today’s tech landscape, and this program is a powerful tailwind for experienced engineers.” — Parag Awadhiya, a 2025 graduate with a Master of Science in Software Engineering.

Westminster faculty are planning to propose a new AI certificate program for the 2027-28 academic year, according to Westminster’s chief communications officer Sheila Rappazzo Yorkin. It will include a core course on generative AI and cover the applications and ethics of AI through an interdisciplinary lens. The certificate will be 15 credits and could be completed in as little as a year. Westminster is also in the process of redesigning certain computer and data science courses to focus on AI.
